# Lab 1.3: Run Your First Query

## What We Are Going to Do
Write a query, read the bytes estimate before running it, then inspect the results, job information and execution details.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Write the query.** In **Studio**, click **+ (Untitled query)** and paste:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT word, SUM(word_count) AS total
FROM `bigquery-public-data.samples.shakespeare`
GROUP BY word
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 10;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Read the estimate.** Before running, look at the green tick at the top right: **"This query will process … when run."** This is the dry-run estimate.

3. **[Console] Run and inspect.** Click **Run**. Check these tabs:
   - **Results**: the top 10 words.
   - **Job information**: job ID, location `US`, bytes processed and bytes billed.
   - **Execution details**: stages, slot time and elapsed time.
   - **Execution graph**: a visual of the stages.

   Bytes billed is at least **10 MB** per table referenced, even for tiny tables.

4. **[CLI] Dry run and run with bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --dry_run \
'SELECT word, SUM(word_count) AS total
 FROM `bigquery-public-data.samples.shakespeare`
 GROUP BY word ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 10'

bq query --use_legacy_sql=false \
'SELECT word, SUM(word_count) AS total
 FROM `bigquery-public-data.samples.shakespeare`
 GROUP BY word ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 10'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Dry run | Shows bytes, costs nothing |
| Top word | `the` |
| Job location | `US` |
| Every action | Runs as a job with a job ID |
